--------                                                                    
                                                                              
  **@pierre** wrote on 2026-10-24 16:22:                                      
                                                                              
  Weighted finite-support feasibility analysis is complete; no production/Rust
  changes or performance runs. Under the same 1024-tap integer-centered       
  symmetric support and 4097-point equal-weight relative RMS grid, the 96 kHz 
  unconstrained optimum RMS is 0.002277016719. Enforcing only the natural     
  configured 500 Hz peak-center magnitude within 0.05 dB has optimum RMS      
  0.002925658226, versus frozen baseline 0.002707278157 (8.0664% higher). A   
  numerical Lagrange-dual lower bound after explicit normal-residual and      
  roundoff allowances is 0.002925658206 RMS. Both positive/negative signed-   
  response intervals are checked; the negative branch is much worse. Thus the 
  anchor pilot RMS nonregression guard already conflicts with this single     
  natural center constraint for this fixed support. At 48 kHz the             
  unconstrained optimum already meets the center constraint and improves RMS. 
                                                                              
  The FFT/CG solve was independently rechecked using direct scalar cosine     
  synthesis and all normal-gradient sums, without FFT or CG in the verifier;  
  normal residuals are below 1.48e-13. This is floating numerical certificate 
  evidence, not an interval-arithmetic proof. It does not prove the original  
  four isolated probe requirements alone infeasible, and no original gate has 
  changed. Dense maximum error also worsens for the 96 kHz constrained        
  optimum, so no designer implementation is proposed. Evidence:               
  audit/artifacts/remaining-fir-weighted-feasibility-                         
  20261024/{README.md,result.json,verification.json,feasibility.py,verify-    
  certificate.py}. Explicit versus opt-in adaptive tap/latency design remains 
  a separate pending user preference.
